paper_id: Wang et al. - 2015 - Connecting the Dots Reconstructing Network Behavior with Individual and Lossy Logs
title: Connecting the Dots: Reconstructing Network Behavior with Individual and Lossy Logs
motivation: Local logs on individual nodes in distributed networks are underutilized; existing log analysis methods cannot handle lossy logs from multiple nodes
problem_framing: Reconstruct network-wide 'event flows' from individual, incomplete, unsynchronized event logs across distributed nodes
key_insight: Implicit intra-node and inter-node event correlations (e.g., send implies prior recv, recv on B implies send on A) can connect FSM-based inference engines to infer lost events
method_signature: FSM inference engine per node; normal/intra-node/inter-node transitions; recursive transition algorithm to infer lost events from correlations
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy of event flow reconstruction; ability to locate packet loss positions and root causes; actionable network diagnosis
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Not all lost events can be inferred by the inference engine
evidence_for_taste: we can also infer lost events
even when there is only one event
the correct ordering for events are also recovered
not revealed until we thoroughly analyze
thinking_moves: 把跨节点的事件关联作为连接日志的隐式锚点，而非依赖同步时钟
从协议语义出发定义'必然事件'，用FSM建模可推导的状态转移
用失败案例(case 1-4)展示传统方法为何失效，而非只证明新方法有效
